config.title: Berlin Cemeteries - FAQ
config.subtitle: Opening rules, travel times from Alexanderplatz, and which of the five fits the afternoon you have.

items.q: Which Berlin cemetery is worth visiting if I only have one afternoon?
items.a: **Jüdischer Friedhof Weißensee, if you have three hours or more, and Dorotheenstädtischer Friedhof if you have less.** Weißensee is 40 hectares with nearly 116,000 graves and needs at least 90 minutes inside plus about 24 minutes travel each way from Alexanderplatz on tram M4. Dorotheenstadt is about 16 minutes door to gate and packs Hegel, Fichte, Schinkel, Brecht and Helene Weigel into 1.7 hectares.

items.q: Is the Jewish cemetery in Weißensee open on Saturday?
items.a: **No. It is closed all day Saturday for Shabbat, and it is also closed on public holidays.** Friday closing is early at 14:30 all year. From April to September it is open Monday to Thursday 07:30 to 17:00 and Sunday 08:00 to 17:00, and from October to March those close an hour earlier at 16:00. Men are asked to cover their heads and kippot are lent at the entrance.

items.q: What is left of the old Jewish cemetery on Große Hamburger Straße?
items.a: **Almost nothing above ground, and that is the point of going.** Berlin's first Jewish cemetery opened in 1672 and held between 3,000 and 12,000 burials before it closed in 1827. In 1943 the Gestapo ordered the graves destroyed and had anti-tank trenches cut through the ground. Today there is a lawn, a low wall, a handful of recovered stones and a replica of Moses Mendelssohn's gravestone placed in 1990. It is open ground with no gate, free, about 11 minutes on foot from Alexanderplatz.

items.q: Where can I see the Berlin Wall inside a cemetery?
items.a: **At the Invalidenfriedhof on Scharnhorststraße in Mitte.** The Wall was built along the ship canal here in 1961 and the cemetery fell inside the border zone, so more than 90 percent of its roughly 3,000 graves were cleared for the death strip, guard towers and patrol road. A stretch of the border wall still stands along the canal side and the Berlin Wall Trail runs past it. Enter from Scharnhorststraße, not the canal. It is open daily, 07:00 to 19:00 from April to September and 09:00 to 16:00 from October to March.

items.q: Are the Brothers Grimm buried in Berlin?
items.a: **Yes, at the Alter St.-Matthäus-Kirchhof in Schöneberg.** Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm lie side by side under two small plain stones that most visitors walk past. The same cemetery holds Rudolf Virchow, the poet May Ayim and the musician Rio Reiser, plus a memorial to the conspirators of 20 July 1944. Café Finovo is inside the grounds. It is about 25 minutes from Alexanderplatz, opening at 08:00 daily and closing between 16:00 in midwinter and 20:00 from May to August.

items.q: Do I need a ticket to visit Berlin's cemeteries?
items.a: **No. All five of these are free to enter.** What varies is the gate, not the price. Große Hamburger Straße has no gate at all, Invalidenfriedhof has one summer and one winter schedule, Dorotheenstadt and St.-Matthäus move their closing time with the month, and Weißensee has weekday, Friday, Saturday and holiday rules. Work backwards from the closing time rather than forwards from your hotel.
